# Best open-ear earbuds for running

Here are the picks that came up most across the reviews, with the review page each is drawn from. I can't browse, so I can't open retailer pages myself. Prices are as listed in the search results and may have changed.

**Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (~$199, list $299)**
- Runner's World ranks it #1. Wired praises the clear sound and the physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-run than touch controls.
- Downsides: IPX4 water resistance and about 7 hours per charge. Runner's World also says Bose has new open-ear earbuds coming soon, so you may want to wait.
- [Runner's World guide with buy links](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) · [Wired guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (list $180, ~$125 at some retailers)**
- It leaves your ears the most open. It has a 12-hour battery, IP55 rating, and physical buttons.
- Wired found the clarity a bit behind the older OpenRun and the Bose. The neckband can clash with long hair, ponytails, and winter hats.
- [Wired review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/) · [RTINGS comparison with Bose](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)

**Best for long runs: Shokz OpenDots 2 ($200)**
- It gets 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and has an IP57 rating. Wired's top overall pick.
- It's pricey. [Wired guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best value: Soundcore AeroFit 2**
- It has an ear-hook design, IP55, 10 hours per charge, and 42 hours with the case. SoundGuys picks it as best budget.
- The sources disagree on price. SoundGuys lists $79.99 at Amazon (MSRP $99.99), while Dealectric lists $129.99 at Soundcore's store, or $104 with code AFSC20. Check Amazon first, since it may be cheaper than the coupon price.
- [SoundGuys list](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/) · [Buy at Soundcore](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2). That link is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you.

**Cheapest way to try the style: JLab Flex Open (~$40–50)**
- Runner's World calls it the lowest-risk clip-on. The sound is less detailed, but it's comfortable and doesn't bounce.
- Runner's World lists both $40 and $50 for it. [Runner's World guide](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

**Other options:**
- **Nothing Ear (Open):** SoundGuys' best overall open-ear pick and best workout pick for running, at about $99 on Amazon. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)
- **Soundpeats PearlClip Pro:** Wired's cheap pick, at $50. [Wired](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Quick guidance:**
- If you want the best sound, get the Bose.
- If you want maximum awareness and a secure fit, get the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2.
- If you're on a budget, get the AeroFit 2 or the Nothing Ear (Open).

Open-ear buds leak sound and don't block outside noise, so they're not ideal for loud gyms. Keep the volume low enough to hear traffic.
